title: 1931 China Floods
summary: From June to August 1931 heavy rain flooded the Yangtze–Huai basin in central China, with eight central provinces worst hit. Estimates of those affected run from 25 to 53 million, and death estimates range widely, up to about 2 million, most from disease and famine afterwards.

uncertainty.note: Flood season June–August 1931 per AMS; aftermath of famine and disease continued later.

where.modern_name: Wuhan, Hubei, China (proxy pin for the Yangtze–Huai flood zone)
where.historical_name: Yangtze–Huai flood zone, central China, Republic of China (pin at Wuhan/Hankou, a proxy)

importance.justification: Described by a scholarly source as one of the deadliest natural disasters on record, affecting tens of millions.

audience_note: Describes mass death from drowning, disease and famine; casualty figures are uncertain estimates.

sources.title: Journal of Climate 36(18), article on causes of the 1931 Yangtze River flood

reviewer_note: Death toll is highly contested (about 140,000 / 422,499 / 625,000 / 2 million); summary gives only 'up to about 2 million'. Pin is a Wuhan proxy for a multi-province flood.
